idea-plugin.name: MavenUp
idea-plugin.description:
IntelliJ plugin for Maven projects to simplify dependency and plugin management. It provides a clear table view of all declared components and enables easy updates to newer versions.

Features:
  • Dependency & Plugin Overview: Displays dependencies, plugins, and the parent POM from all Maven modules, including entries from dependencyManagement and pluginManagement. The <parent> section is listed with type "parent". All tables allow single-row selection only and keep a fixed column order that cannot be reordered.
  • Table Filtering: A text field above the main table filters rows case-insensitively by GroupId, ArtifactId or Property, and combo boxes filter by dependency type, pending version changes, and security findings; all filters combine so only matching rows stay visible.
  • Property-Aware Versions: Shows Maven properties such as ${spring.version} and updates the shared property instead of replacing its references.
  • Repository-Based Update Check: Finds newer versions in Maven Central and configured private repositories, including authenticated repositories from settings.xml.
  • Flexible Version Selection: Select versions from a dropdown, optionally hide unstable releases, and update the affected pom.xml files after confirmation. The confirmation dialog offers a Sync Maven Changes after update option (kept in sync with the corresponding setting) to trigger the IDE's Maven sync afterwards. A green checkmark ("✓") indicates the selected version is the latest; an upwards arrow ("↑") signals a newer version is available. When a different version is selected, the text and the status glyph appear in bold and color; when the current version is selected, they use the default color. Tooltips provide additional status details.
  • Navigation & Context Menu: Jump directly to the definition in the pom.xml via double-click (or optional single-click). Right-click any dependency row for a context menu with Navigate to pom.xml, Open in Maven Repository, or Show Vulnerability Details.
  • Configurable Repository Browser: Choose between MVN Repository and Sonatype Central for artifact version links — applies to both the main table context menu and the Vulnerability Details dialog.
  • Multi-Source Vulnerability Check: Checks direct components and resolved transitive dependencies through OSV.dev, with optional Maven-focused enrichment from Sonatype OSS Index.
  • Detailed Security Findings: Shows deduplicated advisories with severity/CVSS, summaries, sources, references, and clearly marked transitive findings. The Vulnerability Details action is enabled only when a dependency row with findings is selected and opens the findings for that selected dependency. In the details dialog, row-based toolbar actions Open in ... and References... become available after selecting a finding, and right-clicking the selected row in any column except References offers both repository navigation and direct opening of advisory references.
  • Secure OSS Index Access: Stores API tokens in IntelliJ Password Safe, provides a direct link to the Sonatype account page for obtaining a token, and reports a qualified error with a shortcut to the settings when the token is invalid or expired.
  • Global Settings: Configure navigation, automatic version selection, Maven sync after update, unstable-version filters, transitive scans, and optional OSS Index integration under Settings | Tools | MavenUp; settings are stored globally and apply to all projects, grouped into Appearance, Versions & Updates, and Vulnerability Check.
  • Two-Tier Action Toolbar: A top toolbar groups the core actions (Refresh, Find New Versions, Scan for Vulnerabilities, Update) and, separated by a divider, the selection-dependent actions (Open on [browser], Vulnerability Details), with Settings at the end; the Open on [browser] action opens the current version of the selected dependency in the configured repository browser. Toolbar buttons can optionally show text labels instead of icons only.
Background processing and a layered internal architecture keep long-running operations responsive and maintainable. The plugin loads and updates dynamically, so installing or updating it does not require an IDE restart.
